Prevention: Use varieties with some degree of tolerance:
Practice crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops: maize, sorghum, beans, groundnuts, soy beans and cowpeas.
Prune old leaves for good air circulation and to reduce humidity.
Do not do this when wet, as diseases can be spread by people and tools.
Plant new tomato fields away from existing fields with altenative hosts.
Use a dry mulch to reduce water splashes as this spreads the disease.
Apply recommended rates of nitrogen fertilizer as high rates increase the disease.
Monitoring: Monitor tomato plants twice a week for symptoms of the disease, especially in humid conditions.
Look for irregular greasy greyish patches on the leaves which expand rapidly under damp/ humid conditions.
Look for white downy moulds at the margin of affected areas on the lower leaf surface.
Look for brown elongated lesions on the stems.
Look for brown-green blotches or spots on tomato fruits.
When first symptoms are seen, use direct controls.
Direct Control: Remove infected fruits and leaves and destroy by burning or burying 1m underground.
